issues.issue: The grant of the right to transport oil and gas "from the subject and other lands" across the leasehold, surviving the term, conflicts with paragraph 25, under which the Lessee agrees not to assert that right unless the lands are pooled. The two cannot both operate on foreign production.

The term continues so long as gas is "produced or capable of being produced ... in paying quantities, in the judgment of the Lessee"; "paying quantities" is undefined and measuring it by the Lessee's own judgment is open to more than one reasonable reading.

The paragraph extends the term "as provided in Paragraph 7 following," but Paragraph 7 addresses adequacy of consideration and drilling discretion, not the term; Paragraph 6 is the shut-in clause. The cross-reference does not match its target.
"A well shall be deemed commenced when preparations for drilling have been commenced" leaves "preparations for drilling" undefined and therefore unbounded.

Addendum paragraph 16 defines commencement of operations by entry with equipment to build access roads followed by a drilling rig for spudding, a narrower test that the Addendum priority clause makes prevail. The two definitions conflict.

The clause fixes a shut-in payment but never says the payment maintains the lease, which must be read against paragraph 2's habendum requiring production in paying quantities or capability of production. Whether shut-in payments hold the lease is unresolved.

This paragraph reserves "the further right of drilling or not drilling ... as the Lessee may elect," while paragraph 8 provides that the Lessee "shall be required to maintain a well density of at least 1 well per 160 acres" in a unit. Both cannot be given unqualified effect.

"Lessee shall be required to maintain a well density of at least 1 well per 160 acres contained in such unit" reads either as an affirmative obligation to drill or as a limit on unit formation, and "maintain" fixes no time for compliance. The sentence otherwise sits in a clause conferring rights, not duties.

The density requirement stands against paragraph 7's reservation of the right of "drilling or not drilling ... as the Lessee may elect" and paragraph 20's bar on implied covenants. Whether it creates a development duty those clauses deny would have to be decided.

The Lessor's waiver of "notice of any assignment or transfer of the within lease" conflicts with Addendum paragraph 17, which requires written notice of any assignment of a 51% or greater interest within fourteen days, and the Addendum is stated to prevail.

"Any damages if not mutually agreed upon" go to a three-appraiser process and "Arbitration shall be mandatory," yet only crop and drainage damages are enumerated, so the catch-all's reach and the enforceability of the process as an arbitration are undefined.

The Lessor must abide by "all reasonable safety policies of Lessee ... including but not limited to" one setback rule, leaving the general catch-all's reach beyond that specific undefined and unilaterally fixed by the Lessee.

On surrender "the land rental hereinbefore set forth" is to be reduced proportionally, but paragraph 3 makes this a "paid up bonus lease" and no land rental appears anywhere in the instrument. The reduction has no subject matter.

"Force majeure, including but not limited to acts of God, strikes, riots and governmental restrictions" leaves the catch-all undefined beyond the listed events, and whether the extension is only ninety days after the event ends is ambiguous.

The Lessee need only "meet or commence to meet all or any part of the breaches alleged" within thirty days, so what discharges the condition precedent to suit is not stated. Whether commencing to address part of a breach suffices is open.

The extension payment is to be made "in the same manner as provided in Paragraph numbered 6 hereof with regard to the method of payment of shut-in royalties," but paragraph 6 sets the shut-in rate and paragraph 5 sets the method of payment. The cross-reference misidentifies the paragraph.

The bar on reading any "implied covenant, agreement or obligation" into the lease must be reconciled with paragraph 8's express well-density requirement and with the Addendum, incorporated by paragraph 26, which supersedes inconsistent main-body terms. The disclaimer's scope is contestable.

Locations are to be fixed by "mutual consent" with the Lessor's consent not unreasonably withheld, while Addendum paragraph 3 deems approval given if the Lessor fails to return the approval form within thirty days. The two consent regimes are different.

The undertaking not to assert a right to transport gas from other lands unless the premises are pooled contradicts paragraph 1's grant of that transport right "regardless of the source of such production," expressly surviving the lease term.

The clause bites only where there is an "inconsistency" with the main body, and the instrument supplies candidates — Addendum paragraph 16 against paragraph 3, Addendum paragraph 17 against paragraph 11's notice waiver, Addendum paragraph 8 against paragraph 1's storage grant. Identifying inconsistency is itself a construction question.
Restoration "as nearly as possible" to the pre-drilling condition "within 90 days, weather permitting" sets neither a measurable standard nor a firm deadline. Both terms are open-ended.

"As near its original condition as is reasonably possible" states a looser and differently worded standard than Addendum paragraph 1's "as nearly as possible," with no deadline attached. Which standard governs the same work is unclear.

Deemed approval by thirty days' silence is difficult to square with main-body paragraph 23, which requires locations to be fixed by "mutual consent" of Lessor and Lessee. Whether silence supplies that consent would have to be construed.

The covenant that the Lessee acquires no right to drill an underground gas or oil storage well conflicts with paragraph 1's grant of the right of "injecting and storing, air, gas, brine and other substances from any source and into any subsurface strata." The boundary between the two is contestable.

The trigger is a "material adverse change in the quality of Lessor's water supply" "during or immediately after the completion" of drilling, with neither the materiality threshold nor the window defined. Both would have to be construed to apply the clause.

The paragraph ends with the Lessee agreeing to pay the additional costs, taxes, penalties and fines "so levied against the Lessee," although the whole clause is premised on the taxing authority assessing them against the Lessor. As written the promise is self-referential and delivers nothing to the Lessor.

The provision survives only in garbled fragments — a "cash equivalency" payment "times the annualized wellhead price" for an allotment of gas — and states no computable amount. The value of the election cannot be derived from the words.

The clause commutes a free-gas allotment that no other provision of the lease grants; the only free-gas right in the instrument is paragraph 8's gas for one dwelling house on a unit owner's land. The entitlement being converted has no source elsewhere.

Even in fragmentary form the promise of written notice of an assignment conflicts with main-body paragraph 11, under which the Lessor "waives notice of any assignment or transfer of the within lease." Whether notice is owed turns on which provision governs.
